motions.title: Alterations and Additions - Dunkeld Street, Floreat
motions.quote:
Moved by Mayor Shannon, seconded by Cr Haddon-Casey

That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, Council REFUSES the application for proposed alterations and additions and to the existing frontage at Lot 1140 (No. 3) Dunkeld Street, Floreat, as shown on the attached plans stamped received 19 November 2022, the 27 November 2022 & the 30th November the following reasons: 1. The proposal is a non-conforming application under Clause 26(1)(a) of Local Planning Scheme No. 1, as the carport addition and excavation works will be located within the 9m primary street setback area; 2. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed reduced street boundary setback will have an adverse impact on the local amenity due to the increased bulk of the carport within the street setback area, and will not be aligned with the Desired Future Character of the Floreat precinct under Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape; and 3. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed impact of the reduced street boundary setback does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, and will have an adverse impact on the local amenity as the natural topography of the site is unable to be interpreted due to the development not maintaining the traditional street setback. 4. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as the proposed reduced primary street setback would not be respectful of the established character of the Floreat precinct and amenity of the locality due to the visual dominance the carport structure located wholly within the front setback, will have on the established streetscape. 5. If the proposal is approved it may set a precedent for similar street setback incursions to nearby properties, which would alter the existing character of the locality.
